title: The Black Museum
identity_notes: Syndicated true-crime radio anthology hosted and narrated by Orson Welles, using objects associated with cases from Scotland Yard's Black Museum as dramatic frames. The frozen GRH container preserves 32 of the circulating programs. Source logs explicitly warn that surviving titles, program numbers, and broadcast order vary; no episode-specific 1952 airdate is imposed.

eras.label: 1952 U.S. Mutual/syndication circulation
eras.notes: Thirty-nine of the full 52 syndicated programs are documented as airing over Mutual in two 1952 blocks; individual program order is not safely reconstructed.

historical_context.title: International transcription syndication
historical_context.description: The program was prepared as a syndicated transcription series, with U.S. Mutual carriage in 1952 and later international circulation.

historical_context.title: Scotland Yard Crime Museum case-artifact framing
historical_context.description: The series uses objects associated with Scotland Yard crime cases as the frame for dramatized true-crime stories.

historical_context.title: Stable production team
historical_context.description: Orson Welles narration, Ira Marion scripts, Harry Alan Towers production, and Sidney Torch music recur across the matched RadioGOLDINdex records.

historical_context.title: Title and order instability in syndicated preservation
historical_context.description: Surviving logs document title variants, conflicting source numbers, and no safe episode-specific original airdate or order for many programs.
